name: Boxwork and sulfate unit contact
science_objective: Brush, image and analyse bedrock across the southern contact between the boxwork terrain and the layered sulfate unit, and compare it with the sulfate unit north of the boxwork.
why_it_matters: NASA says magnesium sulfates are salty minerals that form as water dries up. Team framing, assumed: a candidate hydrated-sulfate (ISRU water) stop; no NASA yield figure is cited. The sol 4848 image shows sulfate terrain past the contact, not the contact itself.
position_source: PDS PLACES localized_interp.csv v42.0, frame ROVER, sol 4848, site 121, drive 1446 (planetocentric_latitude, longitude; last ROVER row for the sol 4848 image). The same row is in localized_pos.csv, so it is a localized solution, not an interpolated one. This is where the rover was, not the surveyed position of the feature itself. Uncertainty 0.5 m is the PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A §4.4.1.2 expected accuracy of localized rover positions against the HiRISE base map; it does not include the offset between the rover and the imaged feature.
ez_theme: Sulfate unit contact: ISRU water candidate (assumed)

evidence.text: Blog sols 4845-4851: the drive took the rover just over the southernmost contact of the boxwork terrain with the surrounding layered sulfate unit; APXS and MAHLI analysed sulfate bedrock across it.
NASA, 23 Jun 2025: the rover is in a layer rich in magnesium sulfates, salty minerals that form as water dries up.
Position accuracy: localized positions have an expected accuracy of 0.5m compared to the base map (PLACES SIS 1.3 Rev-A, §4.4.1.2).
